I'm still learning, but always excited to challenge myself and see what I can create. For this challenge, I'm working on LUNAR LEGACY , exploring the stories of the equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Excited to learn, experiment and make something meaningful!
summary:
LUNAR LEGACY is a digital space archaeology museum concept that brings the stories of forgotten spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon and Mars back to life. Inspired by NASA's challenge, “Abandoned but not Forgotten,” the project aims to transform mission records into engaging, student-friendly storytelling.

Using NASA mission resources as its foundation, LUNAR LEGACY presents the purpose, achievements, and lasting significance of these space artifacts through a planned interactive archive, mission timeline, exploration atlas, and artifact stories. Instead of viewing abandoned equipment as mere debris, the project encourages visitors to see them as important pieces of humanity's journey into space.

By making space history more accessible and engaging, LUNAR LEGACY hopes to inspire curiosity about planetary exploration and ensure that the contributions of these forgotten explorers are never overlooked.

One Explorer. One Legacy.
details:
Project Details – LUNAR LEGACY

LUNAR LEGACY is a digital space archaeology museum concept designed to explore the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It addresses the challenge “Abandoned but not Forgotten” by turning space mission records into an engaging and accessible learning experience.

How It Works

The project organizes information about abandoned spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments into a digital archive. Each artifact is presented with its mission background, original purpose, major achievements, and historical significance.

The planned platform includes:

  • Artifact Archive: Explore and discover forgotten space equipment.
  • Artifact Stories: Learn why each object was sent, what it accomplished, and what happened to it.
  • Mission Timeline: Understand important events in space exploration.
  • Exploration Atlas: Discover where selected artifacts were left behind.
  • Evidence Room: Access NASA references and supporting information.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNAR LEGACY makes space exploration history easier and more interesting to understand, especially for students and young space enthusiasts. It highlights the scientific contributions of equipment that is often overlooked after a mission ends.

The project aims to encourage curiosity, support informal space education, and inspire interest in future planetary exploration.

Technology Used

The web application was developed using React.js, Vite, JavaScript, CSS, React Router, and structured JSON data. GitHub was used for version control and project development. AI tools assisted with brainstorming, coding support, debugging, and content refinement.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative idea is to approach space exploration from a different perspective. Instead of focusing only on astronauts and successful missions, LUNAR LEGACY tells the stories of the machines that remained behind. It presents them as historical artifacts with their own scientific legacies.

Factors Considered

The project considers factual accuracy, educational value, accessibility, ease of navigation, and responsible use of AI-generated content. NASA mission resources are used as the foundation for research, and AI-generated visuals, where used, are not presented as authentic NASA photographs.

Current Development Status and Limitations

LUNAR LEGACY was developed as a web-based prototype. However, during final testing, technical issues with deployment and page routing caused some website pages to display blank screens or remain inaccessible. As a result, the website is not currently fully functional. The project concept, research, design, planned features, and development approach are presented in the submitted presentation. Further debugging and deployment are part of the ongoing development process.

One Explorer. One Legacy.
